pharm: Orally active, non-aromatizable dihydrotestosterone derivative (1-methyl-DHT) that acts as an androgen receptor agonist; strongly androgenic and weakly anabolic.
quick: Initially 25 mg 2-3 times daily; maintenance 25 mg 1-2 times daily
Contraindicated with liver tumours; monitor LFTs
Prostate exam/PSA, hematocrit, LFTs, blood pressure
summary: Mesterolone (Proviron) is an orally active androgen derived from dihydrotestosterone, used for male androgen deficiency/hypogonadism and historically (with unproven efficacy) for male infertility. It is non-aromatizable, so it does not convert to estrogen, and is not 17-alpha-alkylated, giving it relatively low hepatotoxicity. It is not FDA-approved and was never marketed in the United States; the data here are drawn from EMA/SmPC and BNF sources. It is contraindicated in prostate or breast carcinoma in men and in pregnancy.
indications: Male infertility / oligospermia (historical use; efficacy unproven and feedback suppression may worsen spermatogenesis)

dosage.t: Spread through the day for several months
For ~90 days (one spermatogenesis cycle), then maintenance
dosage.n: Efficacy unproven; may suppress sperm production via feedback

admin: May be taken with or without food
Take at consistent times each day
Intended for use in men only - women and pregnant individuals must not take or handle the tablets
moa: Mesterolone is an androgen receptor agonist that supplements endogenous testosterone. As a 1-methyl derivative of dihydrotestosterone it is non-aromatizable (it cannot be converted to estrogens, so it does not cause estrogen-mediated effects such as gynecomastia) and is only weakly anabolic systemically because it is inactivated by 3-alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase in muscle.
preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy - androgens can cause virilization of a female fetus. Mesterolone is not indicated in women.
lact: Not indicated and contraindicated in women, including during breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution because of the risk of fluid and sodium retention and oedema; no specific dose adjustment is defined - monitor.
hepatic: Contraindicated in patients with liver tumours. Because mesterolone is not 17-alpha-alkylated, its hepatotoxicity is low, but periodic liver function monitoring is advised.

major: Oral anticoagulants (warfarin) - androgens can enhance anticoagulant effect (monitor INR)
Antidiabetic agents - increased risk of hypoglycaemia (may need dose reduction)
minor: Hepatic enzyme inducers/inhibitors - theoretical effects on metabolism
interactions.diagnostics: May suppress clotting factors II, V, VII, and X, and may alter thyroid function tests, glucose tolerance, and lipid profiles.

serious: Stimulation of latent prostate carcinoma or benign prostatic hyperplasia
Suppression of spermatogenesis (oligospermia/azoospermia) and testicular atrophy
rare: Irreversible virilization if a woman is exposed

monitoring: Prostate examination and PSA (especially in older men)
Blood glucose in diabetics and INR in anticoagulated patients
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed; this medicine is for men only - women and pregnant individuals must not take or handle it
Seek urgent care for a painful erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism)
Attend regular blood tests and prostate/breast checks
Report mood changes, swelling, breathlessness, or yellowing of the skin/eyes
Tell your doctor about blood thinners, diabetes medicines, or ciclosporin; this drug may not reliably restore fertility
pk: Androgenic effects over days to weeks
Store in a cool, dry place below 25-30 C
pearls: Not FDA-approved and never marketed in the US - data here are from EMA/SmPC and BNF sources
Non-aromatizable, so it does not cause estrogen-mediated effects such as gynecomastia
Not 17-alpha-alkylated, so hepatotoxicity is lower than with many other oral anabolic-androgenic steroids
Paradoxically suppresses sperm production despite historical use for infertility (negative feedback on the HPG axis)
Classified as a controlled substance (anabolic steroid) in many jurisdictions
missed: Take the missed dose when you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it - do not take a double dose.
overdose: Acute toxicity is low; nausea and vomiting may occur. There is no specific antidote - management is supportive.
